šar-ru-ki-in-i₃-lu-ba-ni: Sharrukin-ilubani (Langdon Šar-ru-ki-in-ì-lu-ba-ni) — first king of the dynasty of Agade, the king known in English as Sargon of Akkad (Šarrukin); ŠAR-RU-KI-IN + NI-LU-BA-NI, which Langdon takes as the rest of one name; the copy marks the surface of NI and LU as damaged, so the reading of these last four signs is uncertain
nu-{ĝeš}kiri₆: gardener, orchard-keeper (Langdon nu-giš-šar) — nu, a prefix forming words for a person's trade, + {ĝeš}kiri₆ 'orchard, garden' (GIŠ.SAR, the SAR sign read kiri₆ after the wood sign)
sagi: cup-bearer, a court office — read as one word, sagi; the signs are Langdon's KA.ŠU.DUG (his ka-šu-duĝ); the first sign as drawn on the copy is unlike its usual KA, and its identification is uncertain
ri-mu-uš: Rimush (Langdon Rí-mu-uš) — king of Agade, son of Sargon; RI-MU-UŠ; an Akkadian name
šar-ru-ki-in: Sharrukin (Langdon Šar-ru-ki-in) — Šarrukin, first king of Agade, the king known in English as Sargon of Akkad; ŠAR-RU-KI-IN; an Akkadian name
ma-ni-iš-ti-iš-šu: Manishtishu (Langdon Ma-ni-iš-ti-iš-šu) — king of Agade, son of Sargon and elder brother of Rimush; MA-NI-IŠ-TI-IŠ-ŠU; an Akkadian name, spelled Ma-ni-iš-te-šu on a Nippur copy
ri-mu-šu-uš: Rimush, miswritten ri-mu-šu-uš (Langdon: 'Sic! Error for Ri-mu-uš-šu') — the king of Agade, son of Sargon, named as Manishtishu's younger brother; the last two signs are in the wrong order
na-ra-am-{d}suen: Naram-Suen (Langdon Narâm-Sin, Na-ra-am-ᵈEn-zu) — king of Agade, son of Manishtishu; NA-RA-AM + the moon-god Suen (EN.ZU, Langdon Sin) with the divine determinative; an Akkadian name; on this prism the god's name, and in its second mention the whole name, are in a break and restored by Langdon
šar-ga-li₂-šar-ri: Shargalisharri (Langdon Šar-ga-lí-šar-rí) — king of Agade, son of Naram-Suen; ŠAR-GA-LI₂-ŠAR-RI (li₂ the NI sign); an Akkadian name; on this prism only the first sign survives, damaged, and the rest is Langdon's restoration from a Nippur copy
a-ba: who? — interrogative pronoun; a-ba-am₃ 'who is it / who was it?'
nu: not — negative particle (the NU sign); before a noun, 'not (a) …'
i-gi₄-gi₄: Igigi (Langdon [I-gí-]gí) — a king of Agade, the first of four named after 'who was king? who was not king?'; I-GI₄-GI₄, the beginning restored by Langdon; other copies have ì-gi-gi and ì-ki-ki
i-mi: Imi (Langdon [I-mi]) — a king of Agade, one of four named after 'who was king?'; on this prism the name is in a break and is restored by Langdon from other copies
na-ni: Nani (Langdon [Na-ni]) — a king of Agade, one of four named after 'who was king?'; on this prism the name is in a break and is restored by Langdon; other copies have na-nu-um
du-du: Dudu (Langdon Du-du) — king of Agade, father of Shu-Durul; DU-DU; on this prism the name is restored by Langdon where his own reign is given, and clear where his son is named
šu-dur-ulₓ: Shu-Durul (Langdon Gimil-dur-ūl) — king of Agade, son of Dudu; ŠU (Langdon's Gimil) + DUR + KIB, which Langdon (after Scheil) reads ul; the name is in a break on this prism and the signs shown are Langdon's restoration; the reading of the last sign is uncertain

__broaden__.e-lu-lu: Elulu — king of Ur; the name is not on this prism, restored by Langdon from other copies · Elulu — also a king of Agade, the last of four named after 'who was king?' (Langdon [E-lu-lu]); likewise not on this prism, restored by Langdon; other copies have i-lu-lu
__broaden__.ur-{d}za-ba₄-ba₄: Ur-Zababa (Langdon Ur-ᵈIlbaba) — king of Kish, son of Shu-Suen; ur 'man, servant' + the god Zababa of Kish, written ZA + the MUŠ₃ sign twice (read ba₄) with the divine determinative (Langdon ᵈIlbaba): 'servant of Zababa'; the first sign, UR, lies in a break on this copy · also the king whose cup-bearer Sargon was, where the name is clear on the copy but has a stray upright wedge after ZA, marked 'sic!' and not read
__broaden__.a-ga-de₃: Agade (Langdon A-ga-dé; Akkad) — city in northern Babylonia, seat of the dynasty of Sargon; A-GA-NE (NE read de₃, Langdon dé) + the place-determinative KI, as a-ga-de₃{ki} · also written without GA (a-de₃, the A marked 'sic!' on the copy) and without KI, at the head of the dynasty
